Traceability Plan Example
- Sprouter (§ 1.1315)
The purpose of this document is to help businesses establish a traceability plan as required in § 1.1315 of
the Food Traceability Rule.
This example includes the information that is required by the Food Traceability Rule and is one example
of how a traceability plan can be established. There is no specific format required for the traceability plan,
but the information in the traceability plan must meet the requirements as described in § 1.1315 of the
Food Traceability Rule and reflect the current practices specific to the covered entity.
Requirements under § 1.1315 of the Food Traceability Rule:
If you are subject to the requirements of the rule, you must establish and maintain a traceability plan
containing the following information:
1. A description of the procedures you use to maintain the records you are required to keep under this
rule, including the format and location of these records.
2. A description of the procedures you use to identify foods on the Food Traceability List that you
manufacture, process, pack, or hold;
3. A description of how you assign traceability lot codes to foods on the Food Traceability List, if
applicable;
4. A statement identifying a point of contact for questions regarding your traceability plan and records;
and
5. If you grow or raise a food on the Food Traceability List (other than eggs), a farm map showing the
areas in which you grow or raise such foods.
• Except for aquaculture farms, the farm map must show the location and name of each
field (or other growing area) in which you grow a food on the Food Traceability List, including
geographic coordinates and any other information needed to identify the location of each field or
growing area.
• For aquaculture farms, the farm map instead must show the location and name of each container
(e.g., pond, pool, tank, cage) in which you raise seafood on the Food Traceability List, including
geographic coordinates and any other information needed to identify the location of each
container.
6. You must update your traceability plan as needed to ensure that the information provided reflects
your current practices and to ensure that you are in compliance with the requirements of the Food
Traceability Rule. You must retain your previous traceability plan for 2 years after you update the plan.
www.fda.gov September 2024

chunks.text:
Traceability Plan Example for Sprouter (continued)
Procedures to Maintain the Records
Digital records of all required KDEs are captured and stored in an excel document on the Traceability
Manager’s laptop. Records are maintained for two years.
Hard copies of Bills of Lading are provided to subsequent recipients containing all required KDEs. Some
companies also receive digital advanced shipment notices containing all required KDEs.
Procedures to Identify FTL Foods
All products packed at this operation are on the FTL.
Assigning Traceability Lot Codes
Lot codes are assigned using sprout type (“AL” or “MB”), harvest date (MMDDYY) and growing location
(“RD1-12” or “MBB1-10”). For example, a lot of alfalfa sprouts harvested on Aug. 19, 2024, from rotary
drum 1 would have the TLC “AL081924RD1.”
Point of Contact
Jen Clover, Traceability Manager, 123-456-7899
Farm Map
See Appendix.
Traceability Plan Updates
This plan is reviewed annually as part of our management review of our food safety system, as well as
whenever something changes in our traceability procedures. Each previous traceability plan is kept in
a folder on the Traceability Manager’s laptop for at least two years after it is updated folder on our local
computer system for at least two years after it is updated.
www.fda.gov 2 September 2024

traceReadyContext.traceReadyScope: FSMA 204 traceability readiness: covered foods, covered entities, CTEs, KDEs, TLCs, traceability plan, evidence links, and sortable export readiness.

coreSourcesToIngest.title: Final Rule: Requirements for Additional Traceability Records for Certain Foods
coreSourcesToIngest.reason: This is FSMA 204. It defines the traceability-record requirements TraceReady audits: CTEs, KDEs, TLCs, traceability plan, record maintenance, and sortable export readiness.

coreSourcesToIngest.title: 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S: Additional Traceability Records for Certain Foods
coreSourcesToIngest.reason: This is the executable legal source for the rule engine. Use sections 1.1300 through 1.1465 as source-backed chunks.

coreSourcesToIngest.title: Food Traceability List
coreSourcesToIngest.reason: Determines whether a product is on the Food Traceability List and therefore whether FSMA 204 records may be required.

coreSourcesToIngest.title: Proposed Rule: Requirements for Additional Traceability Records for Certain Foods: Compliance Date Extension
coreSourcesToIngest.reason: Same traceability docket. Track for compliance-date and regulatory-change monitoring, but do not treat proposed text as final executable rule logic unless finalized or otherwise legally directed.

coreSourcesToIngest.title: Draft Guidance: Questions and Answers About Requirements for Additional Traceability Records for Certain Foods
coreSourcesToIngest.reason: Useful for practical interpretation and customer-facing explanations. It should support reviewer decisions, not override codified eCFR rule logic.

coreSourcesToIngest.title: Small Entity Compliance Guide: Requirements for Additional Traceability Records for Certain Foods
coreSourcesToIngest.reason: Useful for small and mid-sized operator workflows, onboarding, explanations, and examples.

adjacentCustomerRules.title: Standards for the Growing, Harvesting, Packing, and Holding of Produce for Human Consumption
adjacentCustomerRules.reason: Applies to many grower/packer customers and helps interpret farm, harvest, cooling, and packing context. It is not the TraceReady MVP rule engine.

adjacentCustomerRules.title: Final Rule: Pre-Harvest Agricultural Water
adjacentCustomerRules.reason: Important for produce farms, but it concerns water safety standards rather than FSMA 204 traceability-record readiness.

adjacentCustomerRules.title: Current Good Manufacturing Practice and Hazard Analysis and Risk-Based Preventive Controls for Human Food
adjacentCustomerRules.reason: Relevant for processors and manufacturers. Later useful for recall plans and supply-chain controls, but not first-scope CTE/KDE/TLC checks.

adjacentCustomerRules.title: Foreign Supplier Verification Programs for Importers of Food for Humans and Animals
adjacentCustomerRules.reason: Relevant for importers and foreign supplier evidence. Later useful if TraceReady handles imported supplier records.

adjacentCustomerRules.title: Sanitary Transportation of Human and Animal Food
adjacentCustomerRules.reason: Shipment and transportation records may support evidence, but this rule is not the FSMA 204 traceability audit itself.

adjacentCustomerRules.title: Amendments to Registration of Food Facilities
adjacentCustomerRules.reason: Facility registration identifiers may help entity/location resolution but should not drive MVP traceability findings.

adjacentCustomerRules.title: Record Availability Requirements: Establishment, Maintenance, and Availability of Records
adjacentCustomerRules.reason: Relevant to FDA record-access authority, but FSMA 204 has its own specific record and 24-hour sortable-export requirements.

notMvpRules.title: Laboratory Accreditation for Analyses of Foods
notMvpRules.reason: Lab accreditation is not traceability record readiness.

notMvpRules.title: Mitigation Strategies to Protect Food Against Intentional Adulteration
notMvpRules.reason: Food defense and intentional adulteration are outside the FSMA 204 traceability wedge.

notMvpRules.title: Accredited Third-Party Certification
notMvpRules.reason: This governs certification-body accreditation, not TraceReady audit-readiness checks.

notMvpRules.title: Current Good Manufacturing Practice and Hazard Analysis and Risk-Based Preventive Controls for Food for Animals
notMvpRules.reason: TraceReady's current wedge is FDA-regulated human food on the Food Traceability List. Animal food is not on the current FTL.

notMvpRules.title: Information Required in Prior Notice of Imported Food
notMvpRules.reason: Import notice workflow is adjacent only if TraceReady later expands into import compliance operations.

notMvpRules.title: Criteria Used to Order Administrative Detention of Food for Human or Animal Consumption
notMvpRules.reason: Administrative detention is FDA enforcement authority, not customer traceability-readiness workflow.

notMvpRules.title: Implementation of FSMA Amendments to the Reportable Food Registry Provisions
notMvpRules.reason: Reportable Food Registry workflow is not part of the FSMA 204 MVP.

ingestionPolicy: Use eCFR 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S as codified legal truth for executable rule logic.
Use FDA Food Traceability List as product-scope truth.
Use FDA guidance and small-entity guides as interpretation support, not as override authority.
Track proposed rules and compliance-date changes as regulatory-change signals, not final executable rules unless finalized or legally directed.
Keep adjacent FSMA rules as customer context until TraceReady intentionally expands beyond FSMA 204 traceability readiness.
